conventions.convention: Concentrations range over [0,∞); P₀ is the blank law. A positive decision means X>t, and a false negative means X≤t.

An exact critical level satisfies P₀(X>L_C)=α. L_D is the least c>0 satisfying the equality P_c(X≤L_C)=β, when such a least concentration exists. L_C uses response units; L_D uses concentration units.
CV(c)=√Var_c(X)/E_c[X] is used only with positive finite mean and finite variance. k_Q>0 denotes a CV tolerance, and L_Q is the least positive concentration satisfying CV(c)≤k_Q.
Assume AC; σ₀>0; 0<α,β<1/2; k_Q>0. The known-blank response law is N(c,σ₀²), with zero blank mean, unit calibration slope, and variance independent of concentration.
z_q is the unique standard normal quantile satisfying Φ(z_q)=q, for 0<q<1; z_{1-q}=−z_q.
Additional blank-estimation variance is an explicit comparison-model assumption: D_c has law N(c,σ₀²+τ²), with τ>0. It is not asserted for every blank-estimation procedure.
The heteroscedastic scale is σ₀(1+ρc), with ρ≥0. A censored report records the category Y≤L_C, whose likelihood contribution is its event probability.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC, σ₀>0, 0<α,β<1/2, and k_Q>0. For X∼N(c,σ₀²), c∈[0,∞), rejecting the blank when X>L_C, the exact limits are L_C=z_{1−α}σ₀, L_D=(z_{1−α}+z_{1−β})σ₀, and L_Q=σ₀/k_Q.

An exact critical level satisfies P₀(X>L_C)=α; a detection limit is the least c>0 satisfying P_c(X≤L_C)=β, when it exists; a quantification limit is the least c>0 satisfying CV(c)≤k_Q, when it exists.

Assume AC. The standard normal CDF Φ is continuous and strictly increasing, with limits 0 and 1 at −∞ and +∞, and P(Z=x)=0 for every real x. Each q∈(0,1) has a unique real z_q satisfying Φ(z_q)=q, and z_{1−q}=−z_q.
Assume AC. For m∈ℝ, σ≥0, and a real random variable X with law N(m,σ²), E[X]=m and Var(X)=σ².

concerns.concern: Step 1.1 writes E[Z·1_{|Z|≤n}]=∫_{−n}^{n}xφ(x) dx=0 'by [F4]' and [F7]. F4 supplies integration against the law, whereas F7 is a proper Riemann substitution theorem. The passage through integration against the normal density and equality of compact Lebesgue and Riemann integrals is implicit. The published density-integration and bounded-Riemann/Lebesgue bridge theorems supply these routine steps under the stated AC assumption, but neither is directly cited or declared in this item's deps.
